messages:
keisha: Quick coordination thread  I'm proposing a small set of snippet updates for the streaming + pagination doc. Main goals: 1) unify naming (`resume_token`), 2) add small TypeScript type defs for stream chunks, 3) show Go idiomatic channel/read loop, and 4) include a Python sync+async pair.

mohit: Sounds good. Can you also include a tiny TS RxJS example? Some frontend folks use observables and ask about backpressure semantics.

ana: (typo) -> ana: I can do Python. I'll show an async generator and a synchronous iterator wrapper so both users are covered. Also include a short note about partial responses (when token-level output arrives in multiple chunks) and how to assemble them.

keisha: Great. I'm drafting TS and the migration note. Draft PRs: #6230 (TS + migration note), #6231 (py), #6232 (go). I'll try to keep each PR < 10 files.

yuri: For Go, demonstrate context cancellation and an io.ReadCloser style wrapper so users can stream into existing libs. Example snippet to include: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
defer cancel()
ch := make(chan Chunk)
go func() {
  defer close(ch)
  // stream loop reading from client and sending to ch
}()
for c := range ch {
  process(c)
}
```

mohit: TS snippets: include type for chunk shape so TS users get better autocomplete. e.g.: ```ts
type StreamChunk = { text?: string; token?: string; done?: boolean }
``` Also add RxJS example: ```ts
const obs$ = from(streamAsyncIterator(req))
  .pipe(bufferTime(50), map(joinChunks))
```

ana: For Python, I'll show both: `async for chunk in client.stream(...):` and a sync helper `for chunk in client.stream_sync(...)` that wraps the async generator for migrate-to-sync cases. Also add a short glue snippet for concatenating partial chunks safely (check for `chunk.token` boundaries).

keisha: Important migration note: we should provide a tiny compat helper for older SDKs that still accept `cursor`. Suggest adding `compat.get_resume_token(params)` utility in the migration PR so users can call it while upgrading.

mohit: Nice. Also add a short test snippet that asserts the typed TS chunk matches runtime shape (tiny runtime check in JS unit) so we catch doc drift.

docs-bot: (docs-bot) Reminder: link checker will fail on internal-only URLs; keep code blocks <=120 chars per line.

keisha: Thanks. I'll avoid internal links and wrap long lines. Also adding a paragraph about "assembling partial responses": recommend accumulating `text` fragments until `done` or `end_of_message` flag.

yuri: One more: show how to handle resume_token collisions when resuming across model versions (short note: "resume_token is best-effort; incompatible model updates may invalidate tokens"). Keep conservative wording and link to model-versioning doc.

ana: I'll include the conservative note. Also add a small sample for exponential backoff with jitter in Python tests: ```python
import random, time
for i in range(4):
  try:
    async for c in client.stream(req):
      handle(c)
    break
  except TransientError:
    time.sleep(0.1 * (2 ** i) + random.random() * 0.03)
```

mohit: For TS RxJS example, add a cancellation signal using AbortController and teardown in the observable. For example: `new Observable(sub => { const ctrl = new AbortController(); sub.add(() => ctrl.abort()); ... })`

keisha: I'll open PR #6230 (TS + migration note + RxJS sample) and tag @mohit and @ana for reviews. Ana, please open #6231 with the Python pair and partial-assembly guidance. Yuri, please open #6232 for Go and include the io.ReadCloser pattern and context cancellation.

ana: Opening #6231 now. docs-bot already flagging a line-length in a long comment, will wrap.

docs-bot: (docs-bot) PR #6231 opened. Lint: wrap long code lines; Link-check: OK.

mohit: Reviewing #6230 tonight. One nit: in the migration note, mention the compatibility table (v0.9: cursor, v1.x: resume_token) and add an example conversion snippet.

keisha: Will add that. Also planning a single sandbox markdown that shows py/ts/go side-by-side for the migration PR. Should make it easier for folks to see differences.

yuri: Small Go nit: avoid overly large channel buffers in examples; show an unbuffered channel with a short comment about when to buffer.

keisha: Good catch. We'll keep the example unbuffered and add a note about buffering tradeoffs.

ana: CI for #6231 shows a flake in the test harness for backoff; tightening jitter fixed it. Merging after that.

docs-bot: (docs-bot) #6231 CI: flaky test -> updated jitter bounds; CI green.

keisha: Merging #6231 (py). Opening #6230 (TS + migration note). Please review quickly, tagging `docs-easy`.

mohit: Reviewed #6230, left a small wording nit about "partial responses" vs "partial tokens". Also requested addition of a runtime type check helper for TS.

keisha: Addressed nits, added runtime type check helper and sandbox link. docs-bot reports lint warning for a long example line; fixed. Opening #6232 now for Go.

yuri: #6232 opened. Added io.ReadCloser example and context cancellation. Also included a short snippet showing how to convert old `cursor` param to `resume_token` when possible.

docs-bot: (docs-bot) PRs #6230/#6232 opened. Link-check passed. Please ensure code block wrapping.

mohit: LGTM on TS after small doc tweak.

yuri: LGTM on Go after tightening a comment.

keisha: All PRs green. Merging TS & Go now, then I'll merge the migration note which references them.

docs-bot: (docs-bot) #6230 merged. #6232 merged. Migration note will be merged once it builds.

keisha: Merged migration PR with sandbox. Published change note in release notes and added a small compatibility table.

ana: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up if users report issues with partial assembly.

mohit: Great work. Filing a small analytics pulse to watch the page views & support tickets for this doc next week.

keisha: Closing this thread. If anything regresses, start a new thread and ping the docs channel. :sparkles:
